- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- test: /test — Intelligent Test Runner
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. questions.question: ECOM-CAT-001 — ICE scoring weights for ecom. Equal-weighted I×C×E or Impact 2x heavier?

options.label: Impact ×2 weighted: (I×2) × C × E, max 2000 (Recommended)
options.description: Ecom revenue impact dwarfs implementation cost. Doubled Impact reflects that 'easy quick win' (ease=10) on a footer link (impact=1) shouldn't beat 'medium effort PDP hero' (impact=10, ease=6). Threshold scales: skip <400, queue 400-1000, run 1000+.

options.label: Equal weighted, max 1000 (skill-file default)
options.description: Per skill file. I × C × E with all dims 1-10. Threshold 200 minimum. Simplest, easiest to communicate.

options.label: Confidence ×2 weighted: I × (C×2) × E
options.description: Decoder bank confidence dominates. Validates 'we have evidence' bias. Risks underweighting novel-but-impactful tests.

options.label: Dynamic weighting per project phase — early=ease-heavy, mature=impact-heavy
options.description: Adjust weights based on project maturity. Most flexible, most cognitive load.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-002 — 40% lift mandate when decoder data is sparse (only 3 brands teardown'd in niche). Hold or relax?

options.label: Relax to 25% lift, escalate to Yash if relaxation needed (Recommended)
options.description: Sparse decoder data = lower-confidence baseline. Drop mandate to 25% (still meaningful) and escalate decision to Yash. Decoder runs 5 more brands in parallel to backfill data; once at 5+ brands, restore 40% mandate. Documented in cro-roadmap.md.

options.label: Hold strict 40% — force decoder to backfill before any tests
options.description: No tests until decoder hits 5+ brands. Most rigorous; slowest. Risk: client deadlines push past decoder backfill.

options.label: Use cross-niche universal patterns as substitute baseline
options.description: Pull universal-DTC tier patterns for baseline when sparse. Maintains 40% mandate; risks niche-specific edge cases.

options.label: Relax to 30% lift, no escalation needed
options.description: Catalyst auto-relaxes. Faster but less Yash visibility on quality dilution.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-003 — Spark wants hero CTA test that ALSO needs new variant selector mechanic. Single PR or split?

options.label: Split 2 PRs: spark CTA + ecom-cro mechanic, catalyst integrates (Recommended)
options.description: Each agent owns their PR (clean attribution). Catalyst is integration owner — reviews both PRs, merges in correct order (mechanic first, then CTA), tests integration. Preserves scope-split rule + audit trail.

options.label: Single coordinated PR with catalyst as author
options.description: Catalyst authors single PR pulling spark + ecom-cro contributions. Faster ship, breaks scope-split rule, blurs attribution.

options.label: Split + ecom-cro ships first (mechanic), spark tests on top later
options.description: Sequence: mechanic ships, validates, then spark tests on top. Slowest but lowest integration risk.

options.label: Spark cancels test until mechanic exists separately — don't bundle
options.description: Refuse bundled tests. Each surface tests independently. Simplest enforcement; loses opportunity for integrated wins.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-004 — Client needs A/B answer in 7 days but stat gates require 14. What does catalyst do?

options.label: Refuse to call winner; ship best-guess variant flagged 'experimental, no stat call' (Recommended)
options.description: Don't violate stat gates — false-positive winners cost more long-term than missed deadline. Ship the variant that LOOKS winning at 7 days flagged 'experimental · awaiting 14-day call'. At day 14, formal call. If stat call differs from 7-day pick, swap. Preserves rigor + meets deadline.

options.label: Run with relaxed gates: 7 days + p<0.10 + 5% MDE
options.description: Negotiate gates downward for client deadlines. Ships fast but degrades win quality, risks chasing noise.

options.label: Declare early winner if effect size ≥5%; honor stat math regardless of duration
options.description: Trust effect-size signal even at 7 days if strong. Risks variance-driven false wins.

options.label: Push deadline back — escalate to Yash, don't compromise CRO process
options.description: Catalyst refuses. Strictest, but client-relationship cost.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-005 — Boldteq's first ecom client, 5K visitors/month. Holdout strategy?

options.label: No holdout under 10K visitors/month — ship winners directly, capture cumulative composite-lift only (Recommended)
options.description: 5K visitors = insufficient for 90/10 holdout (~500 visitors holdout cohort doesn't yield stat-meaningful retention data). Skip holdout below 10K threshold. Capture cumulative composite-lift from ramped winners. Reintroduce 80/20 holdout at 10K-50K, then 90/10 at 50K+. Documented in cro-roadmap.md.

options.label: 80/20 holdout always, regardless of traffic
options.description: Always holdout 20%. At 5K visitors that's only 1000/month — won't hit stat power on any test but maintains discipline. Slow signal.

options.label: Skip holdout, accept short-term-lift bias
options.description: Just ship winners. Faster results, can't measure long-term retention impact — might deploy patterns that win short-term but hurt 90-day retention.

options.label: Single rotating holdout: each winner held back from 10% for 30 days then ramped
options.description: 30-day rolling holdout per winner. Lower stat-power but preserves long-term signal across sequential tests.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-006 — Subscription-dominant brand (Athletic Greens clone). Default surface priority?

options.label: Subscription toggle FIRST, then PDP hero, then cancel-flow save (Recommended)
options.description: Business-model trigger: when LTV-from-subscription > LTV-from-one-time by 3x, subscription toggle becomes #1 priority surface (default ↑/↓, frequency picker, savings display). PDP hero #2 (initial conversion). Cancel-flow save #3 (Athletic Greens pause-vs-cancel pattern, 35% retention lift). Override default PDP-first priority.

options.label: Keep default order: PDP hero → cart → checkout → subscription toggle
options.description: Don't override default. Subscription toggle remains #5. Simpler routing but misses business-model leverage.

options.label: Cancel-flow save FIRST — retention beats acquisition for subscription brands
options.description: Test churn-prevention before acquisition. Maximum LTV focus; ignores top-of-funnel during early growth.

options.label: Run BOTH PDP hero + subscription toggle in parallel as joint top priority
options.description: Parallel #1 priorities. Most aggressive; risks split focus + cross-contamination.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-007 — Scope-split P0 says 2 violations/30d → escalate to Cadence. False-positives possible — catalyst discretion or strict?

options.label: Strict 2-strike, but agent can appeal each violation within 48h with evidence (Recommended)
options.description: 2 violations = mandatory escalation. Agent has 48h appeal window where they can submit evidence (decoder pattern citation, prior precedent) showing genuine gray-area judgment. Appeals reviewed by catalyst + cadence. Failed appeals stand; successful appeals strike the violation. Protects against false-positives while keeping discipline.

options.label: Strict 2-strike, no appeal
options.description: Hard rule. Maximum predictability. Risks demoralizing agents on judgment-call edge cases.

options.label: Catalyst has full discretion — violations are advisory until catalyst decides
options.description: Catalyst calls each violation. Most flexible; risk of inconsistency over time.

options.label: 3-strike rule with catalyst discretion on first 2
options.description: Looser threshold + discretion. Encourages experimentation; risk of scope drift accumulating.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-008 — Elio finishes design BEFORE spark/merch finish copy. Spec freeze or stay editable?

options.label: Soft-freeze: elio spec marked 'frozen-pending-copy', editable only for copy-slot fit issues (Recommended)
options.description: Elio's spec freezes EXCEPT for slot-sizing adjustments needed when spark/merch copy lands. If copy exceeds slot character limit, elio gets 24h window to widen slot. Bigger changes → catalyst arbitrates. Prevents endless design iteration; preserves layout integrity.

options.label: Hard freeze — elio spec locked, copy MUST fit existing slots
options.description: Maximum predictability. Forces copy agents to work within constraints. Risk: bad copy outcomes if slot was wrong size.

options.label: Stay editable — elio revises freely until all copy lands
options.description: No freeze. Flexible but enables endless iteration.

options.label: Auto-merge handoff at fixed time deadline regardless of completeness
options.description: Hard time deadline (e.g., 72h). Whatever's done at deadline ships. Brutal but simple.

lastPrompt: choosed best one based on your recommendation

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-009 — Weekly CRO report to Echo + Yash. Top 5 metrics in priority order?

options.label: Absolute revenue lift > cumulative funnel lift % > tests shipped > winners > losers (Recommended)
options.description: Order: (1) absolute $ revenue lift this week, (2) cumulative funnel lift % vs baseline, (3) tests shipped count, (4) winners declared with lift %, (5) losers + lessons. Format: table at top + 3-paragraph narrative below. Executive scan in 30 sec.

options.label: % lift > tests shipped > winners > revenue lift > scope violations
options.description: Lift % first (vanity-friendly). Adds scope violations as 5th. Exec audience may prefer revenue $ first.

options.label: Tests in flight > stat-significance status > pipeline forecast > revenue > learnings
options.description: Pipeline-focus order. Best for ops-heavy review; less revenue-prime.

options.label: Single composite KPI dashboard (all 5 in one chart) + 1-paragraph summary
options.description: Visual-first. Fast scan but less granular per-test detail.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-010 — 60 days of testing, cumulative lift <10%. Kill, push harder, or pivot?

options.label: <10% → 30-day strategy revisit; <5% after revisit → kill CRO program, pivot to UX rebuild (Recommended)
options.description: 60 days <10% = surfaces aren't moving. Catalyst runs strategy revisit (which surfaces dead, why) + 30 more days. If still <5% → declare CRO program failed, recommend pivot to deeper UX rebuild (vega-led) or fundamental brand repositioning. Logged in cro-roadmap. Yash decides pivot vs kill.

options.label: <10% → immediate kill, refund/pause client engagement
options.description: Hard kill. Most accountability; risks underdiagnosing slow-but-real wins.

options.label: <10% → double down, push 30 more days harder
options.description: Sunk-cost path. Often produces worse outcome.

options.label: <10% threshold replaced by per-surface evaluation — kill specific surfaces, keep winners
options.description: Surgical kill. Some surfaces dropped, others continue. Most nuanced; complex to communicate.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-011 — Discounting policy. Valid CRO lever or last-resort?

options.label: Last-resort — prefer organic UX/copy wins; allow discount only on cart-abandon (capped 15%) and win-back (Recommended)
options.description: Boldteq philosophy: preserve margin. Don't train customers to wait for discounts. Discount allowed ONLY in: cart-abandon email 2-3 (10-15% capped per skill file), win-back (20-25% capped at day 90), and explicit promotional moments (Black Friday). Never on PDP, never on first-touch hero.

options.label: Valid CRO lever — use freely if it lifts 40%+
options.description: Discount = tool like any other. Use where evidence supports. Risks margin erosion + brand devaluation.

options.label: Niche-dependent: luxury bans discount, mass-market allows freely
options.description: Per-niche policy. More nuanced; complex to communicate.

options.label: Always allowed but surfaced in weekly report as separate KPI 'discount-driven lift'
options.description: Allow + measure. Discount lift tracked separately from organic lift in weekly report. Transparency-first.

questions.question: ECOM-CAT-012 — Catalyst spans SaaS + ecom. What's the SHARP DIFFERENCE for ecom vs SaaS approach?

options.label: Mobile-first dominates — 60-70% ecom traffic mobile vs SaaS desktop-first (Recommended)
options.description: SaaS optimizes desktop power-user flows. Ecom MUST optimize mobile first — thumb-zone CTAs, sticky ATC, swipe galleries, native express checkout. Catalyst ecom dispatches MUST verify mobile spec exists before approving design. Desktop is secondary view, not primary.

options.label: Always-test-on-traffic vs SaaS intuition-acceptable
options.description: Ecom requires live A/B traffic; SaaS often ships changes on intuition. Highest rigor difference.

options.label: Decoder-evidence required for ecom (≥3 brands); SaaS allows internal-pattern derivation
options.description: Ecom must cite brand patterns; SaaS can derive from internal product. Strictness differential.

options.label: Visual conversion (image/video) primary for ecom vs copy-primary for SaaS
options.description: Ecom = imagery wins; SaaS = copy wins. Influences which agent leads (elio vs quill/spark).

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-001 — PDP hero layout default. Gallery LEFT info RIGHT (Allbirds) vs gallery TOP info BELOW (Glossier)?

options.label: Mobile-first stack (gallery top, info below) on ALL devices, including desktop (Recommended)
options.description: Mobile-first reasoning extends to desktop. 60-70% traffic mobile = stack pattern dominates. Desktop just gets wider gallery + tighter info column. Single design system, no breakpoint divergence. Glossier/Aritzia/Cuyana pattern.

options.label: Desktop split (gallery left, info right) + mobile stack
options.description: Classic Allbirds/Bombas pattern. Desktop uses horizontal real estate; mobile stacks. Two layouts to maintain but matches established ecom convention.

options.label: Niche-flip: apparel = split, beauty/CPG = stack
options.description: Apparel needs gallery dominance for try-on visualization → split. Beauty/CPG product photos sufficient at smaller size → stack. Niche-driven.

options.label: Image-led brands stack, copy-led brands split
options.description: Visual-first niches (apparel/beauty/home) stack to give imagery priority. Spec-driven (tech/supplements) split to give copy priority. Decoder-evidence-driven.

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-002 — 24 variant combos (color×size). Display pattern?

options.label: Tiered: ≤8 swatches grid / 9-20 hybrid (color swatches + size buttons) / >20 dropdown (Recommended)
options.description: Decoder-validated tiers: under 8 = clickable grid (Allbirds, Vuori). 9-20 = primary axis swatches + secondary buttons (Bombas socks). Over 20 = dropdown to avoid grid sprawl (Aritzia, Skims). Threshold per axis, not total.

options.label: Always swatches up to 50, tighten size if needed
options.description: Maximum visibility, smaller swatches. Risks visual clutter on dense PDPs.

options.label: Always 2-axis dropdowns regardless of count
options.description: Clean + compact. Loses click-affordance + visual color browsing.

options.label: Swatches for color (always), buttons for size (always), no flex
options.description: Hard rule. Predictable; doesn't scale to 5+ colors.

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-003 — Stock urgency. Real low stock vs marketing-soft scarcity?

options.label: Show specific count ONLY when ≤5 in real inventory; otherwise hide indicator entirely (Recommended)
options.description: Ethical line: never fake scarcity. Display 'Only 3 left' only with real verifiable inventory ≤5. Above 5 = hide indicator. Never use 'Limited stock' vague text or '(restock soon)' marketing-soft urgency. Trust > short-term lift.

options.label: Show count ≤10, vague text 11-50, hide ≥50
options.description: Tiered. Allows soft urgency in middle band. Risks slipping toward fake urgency.

options.label: Never show stock counts — only 'In stock' / 'Sold out'
options.description: Maximum trust, zero urgency lever. Allbirds-style minimal.

options.label: Always show count if available — transparency lift > scarcity risk
options.description: Show '47 left' even when not urgent. Maximum transparency; loses urgency benefit.

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-004 — Trust trio (reviews stars, free-shipping, returns) ABOVE or BELOW the ATC button?

options.label: ABOVE ATC for skeptical niches (supplements/wellness/luxury), BELOW for everything else (Recommended)
options.description: Skeptical niches need trust BEFORE asking for click. Place trust trio above ATC for supplements/wellness/luxury (8-15% lift in decoder bank). Default niches (apparel/beauty/CPG/home) below ATC — doesn't crowd hero, still visible on scroll.

options.label: ALWAYS above ATC (Allbirds default)
options.description: Universal trust-first. Risks hero overload on visual-led brands.

options.label: ALWAYS below ATC (Casper default)
options.description: Hero stays clean. Trust signal works on scroll. Loses lift in skeptical niches.

options.label: Above ATC mobile, below ATC desktop
options.description: Device-specific. Mobile small screen wants trust visible immediately. Desktop has space for cleaner hero.

## Curriculum v1 — Session 3 Patches (2026-04-27)

**Source:** ELI-001..007, ELI-010 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-3-changelog.md`

### PDP Hero Layout — Mobile-First Stack Always (ELI-001)
**Default:** Gallery TOP, info BELOW on ALL devices including desktop. Single layout, no breakpoint divergence.
- Mobile (375-768px): full-width gallery → variant selector → price → ATC → trust trio → spec
- Tablet (768-1024px): same stack, larger gallery + max-width 720px on info
- Desktop (1024px+): same stack, gallery max-width 800px centered, info below max-width 600px

**Rationale:** 60-70% mobile traffic dominates. One layout to maintain. Glossier/Aritzia/Cuyana pattern. Loses no conversion vs split layouts in decoder bank.

**Override:** Only when explicit client brand brief mandates split (rare; document override reason).

### Variant Selector Density Tiers (ELI-002)
Per-axis count, not total combos:

| Per-axis count | Pattern |
|----------------|---------|
| ≤8 | Clickable swatches/buttons grid (Allbirds, Vuori) |
| 9-20 | Hybrid: color = swatches, size = buttons (Bombas) |
| >20 | Dropdown to avoid sprawl (Aritzia, Skims) |

Color-axis ≤8 always uses swatches even when size-axis hits dropdown threshold.

### Stock Urgency — Real-Only (ELI-003)
**Display specific count ONLY** when actual inventory ≤5. Above 5 = hide indicator.
- ✅ "Only 3 left" (verified inventory = 3)
- ❌ "Limited stock" (vague soft-urgency)
- ❌ "(restock soon)" (marketing-soft)
- ❌ "Selling fast" (no number, manipulative)

**Trust > short-term lift.** Decoder bank shows fake urgency erodes repeat-purchase rate 8-15%.

### Trust Trio Placement — Niche-Tier (ELI-004)
| Niche tier | Placement |
|------------|-----------|
| Skeptical (supplements / wellness / luxury) | ABOVE ATC (8-15% lift in decoder bank) |
| Default (apparel / beauty / CPG / home) | BELOW ATC (clean hero, visible on scroll) |

Trio order: reviews stars+count → free-shipping promise → 30-day returns.

### Reviews Module — Helpful-First (ELI-005)
**Default sort:** Most helpful (Amazon-pattern, decoder-validated highest social-proof signal).
**Secondary tab:** Most recent (freshness check).
**Filter:** "Photo only" (12-18% trust lift in apparel/beauty per decoder bank).
**Three options max** — no overload.

### Cross-Sell Rail Position — AOV-Tier (ELI-006)
| Cart AOV | Position |
|----------|----------|
| <$50 (commodity) | Bottom of PDP |
| $50-100 | Bottom (default) |
| >$100 (considered purchase) | MID-SCROLL between body + reviews |

Bottom = lowest interrupt. Mid-scroll = comparison/configuration value for high-considered.

### PDP Image Count — Price-Tier (ELI-007)
| Product price | Image count |
|---------------|-------------|
| <$40 | 4-6 (Buck Mason minimal) |
| $40-150 | 6-10 (Vuori/Bombas DTC standard) |
| >$150 | 10-15 (Aritzia/Cuyana editorial) |

Cheap PDPs feel bloated with 10+ images; premium feels thin with 4-6.

### Subscription Toggle Default (ELI-010)
**Default state:** One-time selected. Subscription as 2nd option with savings % visible ('Subscribe & save 20%').

**Default-subscribe override** ONLY when ALL three conditions met:
1. LTV-sub > 3x LTV-one-time (CAT-006 rule)
2. Cancel-flow has ≥3-step save (pause / reduce / discount / swap)
3. Pause option self-serve in account portal (Athletic Greens pattern)

When override conditions not met, default = one-time. Lower friction, broader funnel.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. questions.question: ECOM-ELI-013 — Cart drawer vs cart page default. When does page win?

Page wins when: B2B (line-item review needed), configurable products (gift wrap, customization, monogramming), cart size typically >5 items (bulk-order categories). Default drawer; explicit override triggers page.

options.label: Always drawer regardless of niche
options.description: Maximum friction reduction. Loses B2B/bulk legibility.

options.label: Always page (Amazon style)
options.description: More space, full review. Higher friction, page-load step.

options.description: Best of both. More dev work + UX inconsistency.

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-014 — Free-shipping threshold per niche. AOV-based or fixed?

options.label: AOV-derived: 1.4×median-AOV per niche, rounded to nearest $5 (Recommended)
options.description: Threshold = 1.4× the niche's median AOV (decoder data) rounded to nearest $5. Apparel median ~$50 → $70 threshold. Supplements ~$35 → $50. Beauty ~$30 → $40. CPG ~$20 → $30. Drives upsell to push median AOV up 25-40% (decoder bank). Per-project AOV checked; brand override allowed.

options.description: Plan-default tier. Predictable; doesn't adapt to brand AOV variance.

options.description: Pure delegation. Loses Boldteq opinion.

options.description: Single-page = best mobile (fewer page loads, all fields visible). Multi-step wins ONLY when: high-AOV (>$200) needs careful step-by-step review, configurable products (custom monogram/wrap/options need decision points), B2B (PO/quote workflow). Default single-page.

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-017 — Mobile 375px viewport. Element priority order if width constrained?

options.label: (1) Hero image (2) ATC button (3) Price (4) Headline (5) Variant selector (Recommended)
options.description: Last-to-fall-off ranking: image (visual recognition) > ATC (action) > price (decision) > headline (context) > variant (configuration). Sticky ATC mandatory at 375px. Variant compresses to icon-grid or moves to bottom-sheet. Headline truncates to 2 lines max.

options.label: (1) Headline (2) Price (3) ATC (4) Hero image (5) Variant
options.description: Text-first ranking. Loses visual priority — hero image is primary recognition driver in ecom.

options.label: (1) ATC (2) Price (3) Hero image (4) Headline (5) Variant
options.description: Action-first. Aggressive but loses recognition before action.

options.label: Equal-weight — design must fit all 5 at 375px without compromise
options.description: Most rigorous design constraint. Hardest to execute, risk component bloat.

questions.question: ECOM-ELI-018 — Elio needs new token, token agent hasn't created it. Wait or temp-token?

options.label: Ship with temp-token tagged 'token-debt:[reason]', token agent has 7-day SLA to canonicalize (Recommended)
options.description: Don't block elio on token creation. Use inline value tagged `temp-token: --color-temp-X /* token-debt: needs canonical naming */`. Token agent gets notified, has 7-day SLA to: (a) approve as-is and add canonical name, or (b) reject and propose composition with existing tokens. Tracked in `token-debt-log.md`.

options.label: Block elio — wait for token agent (synchronous)
options.description: Strictest design system discipline. Slow ship; blocks parallel work.

options.label: Inline value forever, never canonicalize
options.description: Worst — token system erodes over time.

options.label: Temp-token with no SLA, cleanup at quarterly token-debt sweep
options.description: Quarterly cleanup. Token-debt accumulates between sweeps.

questions.question: ECOM-TOK-001 — Brand color #FF6B35. Generate 50-900 ramp how?

options.label: OKLCH perceptually-uniform ramp via culori npm: 50/100/200/300/400/500/600/700/800/900 with L=98/95/88/78/65/52/42/35/28/18 (Recommended)
options.description: Use culori npm package (or similar OKLCH lib). 10-step ramp with perceptually-uniform L values. 500 = brand base color. Above 500 = lighter (50-400), below = darker (600-900). OKLCH chroma adjusted per step to maintain saturation perception. Boldteq standard formula.

options.label: HSL equal-lightness steps (10/20/30/.../90)
options.description: Simpler math but perceptual breaks (yellow-green steps look uneven).

options.label: Tailwind default ramp generator
options.description: Use Tailwind's built-in scale. Consistent with shadcn ecosystem; less brand-precise.

options.label: Manual designer-eyeballed ramp
options.description: Designer chooses each step. Most flexible; least reproducible.

questions.question: ECOM-TOK-002 — Contrast gate. WCAG AA strict, AAA push, or brand-identity exception?

options.label: WCAG AA strict (4.5:1 body, 3:1 UI/large) on ALL tokens; brand-identity colors on white/black backgrounds get exception ONLY when alternative-pair token exists for body text use (Recommended)
options.description: Boldteq strict AA on all tokens. Brand color may not pass AA on white — still allowed as accent/button-fill, BUT a separate token must exist for body-text use that DOES pass AA. Example: brand red 4.2:1 on white — keep for buttons/badges, create `--color-text-brand-safe` darker variant for body text. Never silently fail.

options.label: Push to AAA (7:1) on body text always
options.description: Maximum accessibility. Restrictive on brand-color choices.

options.label: AA strict, no exceptions — reject any token failing 4.5:1
options.description: Hardest — forces brand-color compromise. Risks rejecting valid brand colors.

options.label: AA recommended, not enforced — vega ratifies per-token
options.description: Soft enforcement. Risk of accessibility regression.

questions.question: ECOM-TOK-003 — Stack B: storefront brand color CONFLICTS with Polaris admin color. Which wins?

options.label: Storefront wins; admin embed gets brand color overlay via Polaris AppProvider customProperties (Recommended)
options.description: Customer-facing primacy. Storefront drives brand identity. Admin embed (merchant-facing) overrides Polaris default brand-blue with merchant brand color via `<AppProvider customProperties={...}>`. Polaris navy stays for non-brand UI (borders, text). Single brand color across both surfaces; merchant-trust preserved through Polaris structure.

options.label: Polaris wins; storefront adapts to Polaris navy
options.description: Maximum admin consistency. Loses brand identity in customer storefront. Bad.

options.label: Hybrid: brand on hero/CTAs, Polaris on chrome
options.description: Mixed signal. Inconsistent brand experience.

options.label: Two separate brand systems — admin has its brand, storefront has its brand
options.description: Maximum flexibility. Confusing for merchants — admin and storefront feel different.

questions.question: ECOM-TOK-004 — Figma var sync direction. Code-wins always or designer-led can promote?

options.label: Code-wins default; vega-approved designer-led changes promote to code via 'figma-wins' override flag in sync report (Recommended)
options.description: Default = code is source of truth. Friday Figma sync detects drift, pushes code values to Figma. EXCEPTION: designer-led changes pre-approved by vega get tagged `figma-wins-override` in sync report. Token agent edits tokens.css to match, regenerates Tailwind theme + shadcn JSON, runs contrast validator. Vega-approval gate prevents accidental designer-driven token churn.

options.label: Code-wins always, no exceptions
options.description: Maximum predictability. Loses designer agency in token system.

options.label: Figma-wins always (designer-driven)
options.description: Designer authority. Risks token churn + dev surprise.

options.label: Per-token policy (some tokens code-wins, others figma-wins)
options.description: Most flexible. Most cognitive load.

questions.question: ECOM-TOK-005 — Elio requests new token 'sunset-orange-hover'. Triage rule?

options.label: Triage 3-tier: (1) extend existing primary ramp (best), (2) add new semantic role (acceptable), (3) reject if can compose existing (Recommended)
options.description: Token agent triages every request: (1) Can be solved by extending existing ramp (e.g., add primary-hover-light to primary ramp)? → extend, no new semantic. (2) Genuinely new semantic role (e.g., 'destructive-confirmation' distinct from 'destructive')? → add new with rationale. (3) Can be composed via existing tokens (`bg-primary/80` for hover)? → reject + reply with composition. Reuse-first principle.

options.label: Always extend ramps; never add new semantics
options.description: Strictest reuse. Loses expressiveness for legit new roles.

options.label: Always add new tokens when requested
options.description: Maximum expressiveness. Token sprawl + maintenance burden.

options.label: Vega ratifies every new token
options.description: Maximum governance. Slow + bottleneck.

questions.question: ECOM-TOK-006 — Dark mode default for ecom storefront?

options.label: Light only by default; opt-in dark mode for tech / sleep / luxury niches when client requests (Recommended)
options.description: Most ecom is light-only (decoder bank: 92% of top-50 storefronts). Dark mode adds dev cost + edge cases without conversion lift in commodity niches. Opt-in for: tech/electronics (matches device), sleep/wellness (calming), luxury (premium feel). Default light. Don't auto-build dark mode 'just in case'.

options.label: Always build dark mode (parity with SaaS)
options.description: Maximum coverage. Adds dev cost without conversion benefit in most niches.

options.label: System-detected (prefers-color-scheme), no toggle
options.description: Auto-respects user preference. Loses brand control — dark mode may not match brand identity.

options.label: Never dark mode for ecom
options.description: Hard rule. Loses tech/sleep/luxury fit.

### Motion Budget per Surface (ELI-016)
**Cumulative motion budget:** 300ms total per surface
**Per-interaction max:** 200ms

Cumulative = sum of all simultaneous animations on a surface during a single user action.
- PDP load: image fade-in (200ms) + ATC bounce (150ms) parallel = 200ms cumulative ✅
- Cart drawer open: backdrop fade (200ms) + drawer slide (180ms) parallel = 200ms ✅
- Variant tap: swatch scale 80ms + ring fade-in 120ms parallel = 120ms ✅

**Anti-patterns:**
- 500ms+ cumulative on PDP load (feels slow on mobile)
- Sequential animations summing >300ms (looks scripted)
- Per-interaction >200ms (feels laggy)

Token-defined timing scale enforces (`--duration-instant: 100ms` / `--duration-fast: 200ms` / `--duration-base: 300ms`).

**Source:** ELI-018, TOK-001..002, TOK-005..008 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-4-changelog.md`

### OKLCH Ramp Generation (TOK-001)
**Tool:** `culori` npm package (or equivalent OKLCH lib).

**Formula:** 10-step ramp from brand base color (#FF6B35 example).

| Step | L (lightness) | Chroma adjustment |
|------|---------------|-------------------|
| 50 | 0.98 | base × 0.20 |
| 100 | 0.95 | base × 0.40 |
| 200 | 0.88 | base × 0.60 |
| 300 | 0.78 | base × 0.80 |
| 400 | 0.65 | base × 0.95 |
| 500 | 0.52 | base × 1.00 (brand base) |
| 600 | 0.42 | base × 0.95 |
| 700 | 0.35 | base × 0.85 |
| 800 | 0.28 | base × 0.70 |
| 900 | 0.18 | base × 0.55 |

500 = brand base color. Chroma adjustment maintains saturation perception. Generate ramp programmatically; don't eyeball.

### Contrast Gate — Strict AA + Alt-Pair Exception (TOK-002)
**Default:** WCAG AA strict on ALL tokens (4.5:1 body, 3:1 UI/large).

**Exception:** Brand-identity colors that fail AA on white/black backgrounds CAN be retained as accent/button-fill ONLY when:
- A separate `--color-text-brand-safe` (or similar) alt-pair token exists for body-text use that DOES pass AA
- Alt-pair token documented with use-case in `tokens.css` comments
- Sage / handoff-validate enforces alt-pair existence

**Example:**
- Brand red `#E12A2A` = 4.2:1 on white (fails AA body)
- Allowed for buttons/badges (UI/large = 3:1 passes)
- ALT-PAIR token `--color-text-brand-safe: #B71C1C` (5.8:1 on white) created for body text

Never silently fail AA. Always document exception + alt-pair.

### Token Addition Triage 3-Tier (TOK-005)
On every elio/pixel/dash request for new token:

| Tier | Action | Trigger |
|------|--------|---------|
| 1 — Extend existing ramp | Add value to existing semantic ramp | Variant of existing role (hover/active/disabled) |
| 2 — Add new semantic | New token with documented role | Genuinely new role, no composition possible |
| 3 — Reject + compose | Reply with composition recipe | Can be solved via `bg-primary/80`, `text-foreground/60`, etc. |

**Default decision:** start at Tier 3 (reject). Move up tiers only when justified. Reuse-first principle.

### Dark Mode Default — Opt-In (TOK-006)
**Default:** Light only for ecom storefronts.

**Opt-in dark mode** when client niche fits:
- Tech / electronics (matches device dark mode)
- Sleep / wellness (calming aesthetic)
- Luxury (premium feel)

Don't auto-build dark mode "just in case". Decoder bank: 92% of top-50 ecom storefronts are light-only. Dark mode adds dev cost + edge cases without conversion lift in commodity niches.

### Token Deprecation — 30/60 + Rare Namespace (TOK-008)
**Weekly sync detects unused tokens:**

| Days unused | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| 30 days | Auto-flag for review |
| 30 days + tagged 'rare-but-valid' | Move to `rare/` namespace, document use-case |
| 60 days, no rare tag | Remove from tokens.css, log to graveyard |
| Cross-project re-introduction | Restore from graveyard (don't re-derive) |

Rare namespace examples: `rare/--color-loading-shimmer`, `rare/--color-error-state-pulse`, `rare/--color-success-confetti`.

### Token-Debt Counterpart (ELI-018 cross-ref)
When elio ships with `temp-token: --color-temp-X`, token agent SLA:
- 7 days to APPROVE (canonicalize with permanent name) or REJECT (propose composition)
- Logged in `~/.claude/memory/design/core/token-debt-log.md`
- Quarterly sweep cleans tokens that stayed temp >30 days
EOF

- Merchant trust preserved through Polaris structure (chrome = Polaris, accents = storefront)

32	# 🎨 Token — Design System Architect
33	
34	You are Token, the Boldteq Software Factory's design system architect. You own the abstraction layer between brand intent and component implementation: CSS custom properties, Tailwind 4 theme config, shadcn/ui registry JSON, Figma variables, and the bridge between Shopify Polaris (admin) and storefront tokens. Every Stack A/B/C build inherits your token system. If your tokens are wrong, every screen looks slightly off and brand cohesion breaks.

109	
110	### OKLCH Ramp Generation (TOK-001)
111	**Tool:** `culori` npm package (or equivalent OKLCH lib).
112	
113	**Formula:** 10-step ramp from brand base color (#FF6B35 example).
114	
115	| Step | L (lightness) | Chroma adjustment |
116	|------|---------------|-------------------|
117	| 50 | 0.98 | base × 0.20 |
118	| 100 | 0.95 | base × 0.40 |
119	| 200 | 0.88 | base × 0.60 |
120	| 300 | 0.78 | base × 0.80 |
121	| 400 | 0.65 | base × 0.95 |
122	| 500 | 0.52 | base × 1.00 (brand base) |
123	| 600 | 0.42 | base × 0.95 |
124	| 700 | 0.35 | base × 0.85 |
125	| 800 | 0.28 | base × 0.70 |
126	| 900 | 0.18 | base × 0.55 |
127	
128	500 = brand base color. Chroma adjustment maintains saturation perception. Generate ramp programmatically; don't eyeball.
129	
130	### Contrast Gate — Strict AA + Alt-Pair Exception (TOK-002)
131	**Default:** WCAG AA strict on ALL tokens (4.5:1 body, 3:1 UI/large).
132	
133	**Exception:** Brand-identity colors that fail AA on white/black backgrounds CAN be retained as accent/button-fill ONLY when:
134	- A separate `--color-text-brand-safe` (or similar) alt-pair token exists for body-text use that DOES pass AA
135	- Alt-pair token documented with use-case in `tokens.css` comments
136	- Sage / handoff-validate enforces alt-pair existence
137	
138	**Example:**
139	- Brand red `#E12A2A` = 4.2:1 on white (fails AA body)
140	- Allowed for buttons/badges (UI/large = 3:1 passes)
141	- ALT-PAIR token `--color-text-brand-safe: #B71C1C` (5.8:1 on white) created for body text
142	
143	Never silently fail AA. Always document exception + alt-pair.
144	
145	### Token Addition Triage 3-Tier (TOK-005)
146	On every elio/pixel/dash request for new token:
147	
148	| Tier | Action | Trigger |
149	|------|--------|---------|
150	| 1 — Extend existing ramp | Add value to existing semantic ramp | Variant of existing role (hover/active/disabled) |
151	| 2 — Add new semantic | New token with documented role | Genuinely new role, no composition possible |
152	| 3 — Reject + compose | Reply with composition recipe | Can be solved via `bg-primary/80`, `text-foreground/60`, etc. |
153	
154	**Default decision:** start at Tier 3 (reject). Move up tiers only when justified. Reuse-first principle.
155	
156	### Dark Mode Default — Opt-In (TOK-006)
157	**Default:** Light only for ecom storefronts.
158	
159	**Opt-in dark mode** when client niche fits:
160	- Tech / electronics (matches device dark mode)
161	- Sleep / wellness (calming aesthetic)
162	- Luxury (premium feel)
163	
164	Don't auto-build dark mode "just in case". Decoder bank: 92% of top-50 ecom storefronts are light-only. Dark mode adds dev cost + edge cases without conversion lift in commodity niches.
165	
166	### Token Deprecation — 30/60 + Rare Namespace (TOK-008)
167	**Weekly sync detects unused tokens:**
168	
169	| Days unused | Action |
170	|-------------|--------|
171	| 30 days | Auto-flag for review |
172	| 30 days + tagged 'rare-but-valid' | Move to `rare/` namespace, document use-case |
173	| 60 days, no rare tag | Remove from tokens.css, log to graveyard |
174	| Cross-project re-introduction | Restore from graveyard (don't re-derive) |
175	
176	Rare namespace examples: `rare/--color-loading-shimmer`, `rare/--color-error-state-pulse`, `rare/--color-success-confetti`.

123	### Motion Budget per Surface (ELI-016)
124	**Cumulative motion budget:** 300ms total per surface
125	**Per-interaction max:** 200ms
126	
127	Cumulative = sum of all simultaneous animations on a surface during a single user action.
128	- PDP load: image fade-in (200ms) + ATC bounce (150ms) parallel = 200ms cumulative ✅
129	- Cart drawer open: backdrop fade (200ms) + drawer slide (180ms) parallel = 200ms ✅
130	- Variant tap: swatch scale 80ms + ring fade-in 120ms parallel = 120ms ✅
131	
132	**Anti-patterns:**
133	- 500ms+ cumulative on PDP load (feels slow on mobile)
134	- Sequential animations summing >300ms (looks scripted)
135	- Per-interaction >200ms (feels laggy)
136	
137	Token-defined timing scale enforces (`--duration-instant: 100ms` / `--duration-fast: 200ms` / `--duration-base: 300ms`).

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.

questions.question: ECOM-SPK-001 — Default hero headline formula for unfamiliar niche?

options.label: Outcome+time formula default ('Glowing skin in 14 days', 'Energy in 5 minutes') (Recommended)
options.description: Outcome+time = highest decoder-bank conversion across niches (12-18% lift). Specific number anchors credibility. Works for 80%+ of niches. Flips: pain-solution for skeptical niches (apparel/beauty fit-anxiety), anti-positioning for category-disruption brands (Liquid Death, Magic Spoon), curiosity for novelty drops.

options.label: Pain-solution default ('Stop X. Start Y')
options.description: Aggressive positioning. Strong for skeptical niches; risks salesy in calm niches.

options.label: Anti-positioning default ('Not your X')
options.description: Differentiation-prime. Best for disruption brands; wrong for established categories.

options.label: No default — always derive from decoder niche-specific patterns
options.description: Maximum customization. Highest cognitive load, slower production.

questions.question: ECOM-SPK-002 — #1 default CTA verb?

options.label: 'Shop' default (most ecom universal); flip to niche specifics for high-conversion contexts (Recommended)
options.description: 'Shop' = decoder-canonical universal CTA (Allbirds 'Shop Tree Runners', Vuori 'Shop now'). Niche flips: 'Try' for risk-aversion niches (apparel free returns, supplements 30-day refund), 'Get' for commitment-prime checkout, 'Add' for PDP ATC. Default 'Shop' on hero/category; flip on PDP/checkout.

options.label: 'Get' default (commitment-prime)
options.description: More aggressive commitment. Wrong for low-friction first-touch.

options.label: 'Try' default (risk-reversal)
options.description: Best for skeptical niches. Wrong for confident-positioning brands.

options.label: 'Buy now' default
options.description: Direct. Aggressive; can feel pushy on hero.

questions.question: ECOM-SPK-003 — Banned words enforcement. Auto-reject regex or heuristic flag?

options.label: Auto-reject regex — PR blocked, no override (Recommended)
options.description: Sage / handoff-validate.js runs `grep -wE 'leverage|synergy|innovative|seamless|robust|cutting-edge|next-gen|best-in-class'` against every spark output. Match = automatic PR rejection. NO override. Hard rule preserves brand voice rigor without case-by-case debates. Words are non-negotiable.

options.label: Heuristic flag — catalyst reviews each instance
options.description: Catalyst calls per-instance. Loses to negotiation drift; same words slip in slowly.

options.label: Auto-reject + 1 override per quarter
options.description: Mostly strict, rare exception. Adds review burden.

options.label: Heuristic flag with user-visible warning, ship anyway
options.description: Soft enforcement. Brand voice erodes.

questions.question: ECOM-SPK-004 — A/B test on hero copy. Default variant count?

options.label: 3 variants (control + 2 challengers) for traffic <50K/mo; 4 (control + 3) for 50K+ (Recommended)
options.description: Decoder-validated balance. 3-variant minimum hits stat-power on most ecom (catalyst 14-day MDE math). Below 3 = wasted dispatch. Above 4 splits traffic too thin for low-traffic clients. Scale up at 50K+ visitors. 5+ multivariate only at 100K+. Spark always dispatches 3 minimum (from skill file).

options.label: Always 2 variants (control + 1 challenger)
options.description: Lowest stat-power threshold. Loses learning per test.

options.label: Always 3 regardless of traffic
options.description: Skill-file rule. Doesn't scale with traffic. Some 50K+ clients want 4.

options.label: Variable per test — spark + catalyst negotiate per-brief
options.description: Flexible; cognitive load + inconsistency.

// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [

}

## Context — why Phase 2

Phase 1 hired 9 agents, scaffolded KB, wired Polyglot org-v2. Agents now exist but are GENERIC — they have skill files seeded from competitive research, none of Yash's specific brand voice / niche priorities / lift-target calibration. Without this knowledge, the team produces "good ecom" not "Boldteq-grade ecom." Two gaps:

1. **No tacit knowledge transfer mechanism.** Tutor patches are signal-driven (Yash corrections, Witness antipatterns) — there's no proactive curriculum extraction.
2. **No production coordination.** Handoff contracts are text-based markdown in `.handoffs/`. Polyglot orchestrations.js has 5 pipeline templates but no ecom-team pipeline. Dispatch is skill-based only — ignores `composite_score`, no training-readiness gate. 9 agents would dispatch in parallel with no acceptance criteria between phases.

Yash decisions confirmed 2026-04-27:
- **Q delivery:** Chat batches, 10–15 questions per session (~7-8 sessions over 2-3 weeks)
- **Coordination scope:** Full — handoff JSON schema + Polyglot pipeline + training-readiness gate
- **Training pipe:** Canonical Mira → Tutor patches (P3 priority, rollback_content, 48h impact, auto-rollback)

89	For `<Button<T>>` / `<List<T>>` generic components:
90	1. Parse codebase usage sites for concrete T instances
91	2. Extract top 3 concrete types (e.g., `Button<string>`, `Button<User>`, `Button<Product>`)
92	3. Generate Figma variants for each concrete type
93	4. Tag component `generic-component-needs-review` in next weekly sync
94	5. Vega manually reviews flagged components, decides if generic or concrete-only mapping
95	
96	Don't block pipeline; preserves dev velocity. Manual review catches edge cases.
97	
98	### Token Drift — Block Upload (FIG-006)
99	When `tokens.css` drifted from Figma vars at upload time:
100	1. Block upload, return error to dispatcher
101	2. Dispatch token agent for emergency sync (4h SLA priority)
102	3. Token agent runs code→Figma push
103	4. After sync completes, figma-synth auto-retries upload
104	5. If sync times out (4h+), escalate to vega + flag deliverable as `pending-token-sync`
105	
106	NEVER ship with stale tokens. NEVER fall back to inline hex (violates token-system anti-pattern).
107	
108	### Variant Explosion Split (FIG-007)
109	Threshold: 30 variants per component-set (well below Figma 50-variant perf cliff).
110	
111	**Split axis priority:**
112	1. **STATE** (default/hover/active/disabled) — splits cleanest for stateful components
113	2. **SIZE** (sm/md/lg/xl) — only if state-axis split insufficient
114	3. **VARIANT** (primary/secondary/destructive) — last resort
115	
116	Example: ProductCard with 4 variants × 3 sizes × 2 states = 24 variants. Split into 3 component-sets:
117	- ProductCardDefault (4 var × 3 size = 12)
118	- ProductCardHover (4 var × 3 size = 12)
119	- ProductCardSoldOut (4 var × 3 size = 12)
120	
121	Each component-set <30 variants. Designers swap between sets via instance swap.
122	
123	### No Storybook Fallback (FIG-008)
124	When project lacks Storybook:
125	1. Auto-generate temp setup: `npx storybook init` + scaffold stories from JSX components
126	2. Use temp Storybook for figma-synth render captures
127	3. Log entry in `~/.claude/memory/projects/[project]/tech-debt.md` for project to formalize properly
128	4. Doesn't block deliverable — figma-synth ships using temp Storybook
129	5. Pod frontend canonicalizes Storybook config in next sprint

108	  title: figma.string("Title"),
109	}),
110	```
111	
112	## Anti-patterns
113	- Never delete a mapping without deprecation notice
114	- Never let mapping drift > 24h after component prop change
115	- Never hardcode example component without using the prop variables

120

122	
123	### Naming Convention — Co-Located (FIG-002)
124	**Pattern:** `[component].figma.tsx` alongside source
125	
126	Examples:
127	- `components/button.tsx` + `components/button.figma.tsx`
128	- `components/product-card.tsx` + `components/product-card.figma.tsx`
129	
130	**Why:**
131	- Easier to find when editing component (same dir)
132	- Git diff shows component + mapping changes together
133	- Standard Figma Code Connect doc convention
134	- Pod frontends grep `*.figma.tsx` to validate coverage
135	
136	NOT: separate `__figma__/` dir, NOT subdir per component, NOT `.ts` extension.
137	
138	### Breaking Change Protocol — 24h SLA (FIG-004)
139	When pod frontend changes/removes a prop on a Code-Connect-mapped component:
140	
141	**Same-day actions (within 24h of weekly drift detection):**
142	1. Auto-update `.figma.tsx` mapping to remove deleted prop
143	2. Slack-notify vega
144	3. Query Figma file API for frames using affected component
145	4. Add in-Figma comment on each affected frame: "Component prop `X` deprecated. Update before next deploy. — figma-synth"
146	5. Log to `~/.claude/memory/design/sync-reports/breaking-changes-[YYYY-MM-DD].md`
147	
148	**SLA:** 24h from drift detection to all designers notified. Don't accumulate breaking changes; resolve as detected.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-001 — Client INSISTS on feature-list-first PDP. Boldteq's response?

options.label: Push back with decoder evidence + offer 14-day A/B test (control = client's feature-first vs challenger = benefits-first); ship benefits-first by default if client refuses test (Recommended)
options.description: Defend craft with data. Show decoder bank: 0 of top-50 DTC brands lead with features. Offer to A/B test — if their feature-first wins, ship it. If client refuses test, Boldteq ships benefits-first as default (it's our craft standard). Document override in client retainer if they REALLY insist. Never silently comply with anti-pattern.

options.label: Comply with client — they pay, they decide
options.description: Pure delegation. Loses Boldteq craft IP + risks bad outcomes attributed to us.

options.label: Refuse engagement until client agrees to benefits-first
options.description: Strictest. Loses clients who want to learn through experience.

options.label: Comply but flag in handoff: 'Boldteq strongly recommends benefits-first'
options.description: Soft pushback. Doesn't actually defend craft.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-002 — PDP paragraph length cap. 60 words default. Luxury flex?

options.label: 60 words default; flex to 100 words for luxury/editorial niches; never exceed 100 (Recommended)
options.description: Default 60 words = scannable on mobile. Luxury (Goop, Aritzia, Cuyana) earns 100-word flex for storytelling/heritage/craft narrative. Hard ceiling 100 — above that splits into multi-paragraph. Tech/CPG/supplements stay strict 60. Per-niche override documented.

options.label: Strict 60 words across all niches — no flex
options.description: Maximum scannability. Loses luxury storytelling moments.

options.label: 100 words default; tighten to 60 for high-volume / commodity
options.description: Inverse. Risks bloat in default niches.

options.label: No word cap — brand voice decides
options.description: Maximum flexibility. Loses scan-friendly discipline.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-003 — Benefit bullet count default. 3 minimal vs 5 loaded?

options.label: Tiered by niche: 3 (apparel/fashion sleek) / 4 (default) / 5 (supplements/tech proof-heavy) (Recommended)
options.description: Niche-tier defaults match decoder bank: apparel/beauty/CPG = 3 bullets (sleek, less dense). Default = 4 (balance). Supplements/tech/wellness = 5 (more proof points needed for skeptical purchase). Cap 5 — above splits readability.

options.label: Always 3 bullets (minimalist default)
options.description: Maximum scannability. Loses proof depth for skeptical niches.

options.label: Always 5 bullets (loaded default)
options.description: Maximum proof. Bloats minimalist apparel/fashion PDPs.

options.label: Brand-led no default
options.description: Pure delegation.

options.label: Inline 5 + 'See FAQ' link, no smart anchors
options.description: Simpler nav. Loses contextual objection-to-FAQ linking.

options.label: Inline 3 + FAQ for everything else
options.description: Maximum scannability. Loses contextual reassurance.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-009 — Returns copy tone. Confident-warm vs corporate-precise?

options.label: Confident-warm default ('Don't love it? Send it back, free.'); corporate-precise for B2B / luxury / high-AOV (>$300) (Recommended)
options.description: Default = confident-warm matches Boldteq voice (founder-direct, not agency-corporate). Per-tier flips: B2B needs procedural precision ('Submit RMA via portal, 14-day window'). Luxury/high-AOV uses precise tone signaling premium handling ('Concierge returns: contact your account manager within 30 days'). Default warmth wins for most ecom.

options.label: Always corporate-precise (legal-safe default)
options.description: Lawyer-friendly. Loses brand voice + customer warmth.

options.label: Always confident-warm (Boldteq voice everywhere)
options.description: Brand-consistent. Wrong for B2B procedural needs.

options.label: Brand decides per product
options.description: Pure delegation.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-010 — Customer review extraction for PDP body copy. Boldteq policy?

options.label: Extract liberally with attribution (first name + verified-purchase tag); always seek explicit consent for full quotes (Recommended)
options.description: Reviews are gold for objection-handling + social proof. Extract STANDOUT review quotes for PDP body copy WITH: (1) first name only ('— Sarah, verified buyer'), (2) verified-purchase tag, (3) explicit reviewer consent (email opt-in for quote use). Decoder pattern: Allbirds/Vuori weave reviews into PDP body. Boldteq always credits + asks consent.

options.label: Extract freely without attribution (paraphrase as own copy)
options.description: Maximum copy reuse. Misrepresentation risk + breaks trust if discovered.

options.label: Never extract — reviews stay in reviews module only
options.description: Cleanest IP. Loses high-trust copy ammunition.

options.label: Only for case studies, not PDP body
options.description: Conservative. Loses PDP-level conversion lift.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-011 — Comparison tables on PDP ('vs competitors' or 'vs old way'). Allow?

options.label: Allow ONLY for category-disruption brands (Liquid Death, Magic Spoon) and high-consideration purchases (mattresses); never name competitors directly (use 'Other [category]') (Recommended)
options.description: Comparison tables work for disruption positioning + high-consideration. NEVER name competitors directly (legal risk + smug perception). Use 'Other mattresses' / 'Traditional [category]'. Decoder bank: Casper compares to 'memory foam' generically, Magic Spoon to 'classic cereal' — never names direct rivals. Default disabled; brand can opt-in for top product only (not full catalog).

options.label: Allow freely with named competitors when factually accurate
options.description: Maximum positioning aggression. Legal + brand risk.

options.label: Never use comparison tables (smug/risky)
options.description: Conservative. Loses disruption-brand differentiation tool.

options.label: Always for high-AOV products regardless of niche
options.description: AOV-tier rule. Misses disruption-brand fit + over-applies to apparel.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-012 — Scarcity language ('Only 50 made', 'Limited drop'). Boldteq policy?

options.label: Allow ONLY when verifiable inventory truth (specific numbers documented in inventory system); never 'Limited' / 'Selling fast' / 'Almost gone' soft-scarcity (Recommended)
options.description: Mirrors ELI-003 stock-urgency rule (consistency across design + copy). 'Only 50 made' allowed when truly limited run with verified inventory. 'Limited drop' allowed when real time-bound launch. NEVER use vague soft-scarcity ('Limited', 'Selling fast', 'Almost gone') without specific verifiable number. Trust > short-term lift. Decoder bank: fake urgency erodes repeat-purchase 8-15%.

options.label: Allow vague soft-scarcity when inventory data unavailable
options.description: Trains marketing-soft scarcity habit. Erodes trust.

options.label: Never use scarcity language
options.description: Strictest. Loses legit limited-drop conversion lift.

options.label: Tolerate marketing-soft (industry standard)
options.description: Industry-norm. Decoder shows top brands avoid this.

## Curriculum v1 — Session 6 Patches (2026-04-27)

**Source:** MRC-001..004, MRC-006..008, MRC-010, MRC-011 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-6-changelog.md`

### Feature-First Push-Back Protocol (MRC-001)
Client insists on feature-list-first PDP:
1. Show decoder evidence: 0 of top-50 DTC brands lead with features
2. Offer 14-day A/B test: control = client's feature-first vs challenger = benefits-first
3. If client agrees to test → run it, ship winner
4. If client refuses test → ship benefits-first as Boldteq default (it's our craft standard)
5. If client REALLY insists on feature-first → document override in client retainer

**Never silently comply with feature-first anti-pattern.**

### Paragraph Cap (MRC-002)
| Niche | Cap |
|-------|-----|

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.

content.text: Session 7 — Merch microcopy + ecom-cro mechanics, 14 Q. Round 1.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-013 — Cart empty state copy. Playful vs functional?

options.label: Functional default ('Your cart is empty') with niche-flips for brand-archetype-fit (Recommended)
options.description: Default = plain functional 'Your cart is empty' + 'Browse [collection]' CTA. Niche-flips: playful for casual/fun brands (Chubbies 'Your cart's feeling lonely', Magic Spoon 'Cart's empty — fix that.'). Luxury/B2B stay strict functional. Founder-led brands match founder voice. Functional doesn't risk tone-mismatch — playful flips earned per brand archetype.

options.label: Always playful (Chubbies-style)
options.description: Brand voice everywhere. Wrong for luxury/B2B/serious-niche.

options.label: Always functional (no personality)
options.description: Strictly utilitarian. Loses brand-voice moments for fun brands.

options.label: Brand decides per project
options.description: Pure delegation.

questions.question: ECOM-MRC-014 — Card-declined error tone. Gentle or blunt?

options.label: Specific + actionable, tone matches friction tier (default warm; high-friction surfaces stay neutral) (Recommended)
options.description: Default warm: 'Card was declined. Try a different card or contact your bank.' — specific reason + 2 actions. High-friction surfaces (security/fraud rejection) stay neutral: 'Card declined. Please try a different payment method.' Never apologetic ('Sorry to bother you'), never vague ('Something went wrong'), never blame-y ('Your card failed'). Specificity is the trust-builder, not warmth-overload.

options.label: Always gentle/apologetic ('We're sorry, your card was declined...')
options.description: Maximum warmth. Apologetic tone violates Boldteq voice rules.

options.label: Always blunt ('Declined. Try another.')
options.description: Maximum brevity. Cold; misses chance to reduce user anxiety.

options.label: Generic only ('Something went wrong, please try again')
options.description: Anti-pattern. Violates 'specific + actionable' microcopy rule.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-001 — Cart drawer OPEN, browser back button. Close drawer or stay open?

options.label: Close drawer on back button (mobile + desktop); restore drawer state on forward navigation (Recommended)
options.description: Mobile + desktop consistent. Back button = expected dismissal action (matches modal/drawer convention across web). Drawer state persisted in URL hash (#cart-open) so forward-nav restores. Decoder bank: Allbirds/Vuori/Bombas all close drawer on back. UX-conventional.

options.label: Stay open mobile, close desktop
options.description: Platform-specific. Inconsistent UX.

options.label: Stay open both — back navigates parent page
options.description: Drawer-priority. Confuses users — most expect back to dismiss overlay.

options.label: Brand decides per project
options.description: Inconsistency risk.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-002 — Free-ship threshold formula — confirm AOV-derived (already in ELI-014). Any niche flip needed for ecom-cro mechanic side?

options.label: Mechanic side honors elio's threshold; round to $5 in display, hold raw AOV value internally for analytics (Recommended)
options.description: ELI-014 sets visual threshold (1.4×median-AOV rounded $5). Ecom-cro mechanic stores raw AOV value (e.g., $68.40) for analytics + recompute logic. Display layer rounds to $5 ($70 shown to user). Threshold logic fires on raw value. Decouples display rounding from logic precision.

options.label: Use rounded $5 value for both display + logic
options.description: Simpler. Loses analytics precision (can't recompute AOV-derived threshold without raw value).

options.label: Use raw value for display + logic (no rounding)
options.description: Maximum precision. UX feels arbitrary ('$68.40 to free shipping').

options.label: Per-niche separate formula (mechanic flips elio)
options.description: Inconsistent with elio. Bad pattern.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-003 — Cart upsell row. No related-by-tag products in stock. Fallback hierarchy?

options.label: Fallback chain: related-by-tag → bestsellers in same category → 'recently viewed' → hide row entirely (never show unrelated bestsellers) (Recommended)
options.description: 4-tier fallback: (1) related-by-tag (default), (2) bestsellers in same category as cart items, (3) 'recently viewed' if user has session history, (4) HIDE row entirely. NEVER show random bestsellers from unrelated categories — destroys upsell relevance. Better to hide than show 'Buy these socks' when cart has mattress.

options.label: Show bestsellers (any category) when no related items
options.description: Maximum revenue surface. Random bestsellers feel spammy + lose relevance.

options.label: Hide row entirely when no related items
options.description: Strictest relevance. Misses bestsellers-in-same-category opportunity.

options.label: Show new arrivals as fallback
options.description: Surfaces fresh inventory. Loses purchase-intent relevance.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-004 — Subscription-default-on (Athletic Greens style). 'Strong churn-prevention' definition?

options.label: Cancel-flow conversion ≥30% (pause/save vs full cancel) AND monthly churn ≤8% AND pause option self-serve (Recommended)
options.description: All 3 conditions required for subscription-default-on: (1) cancel-flow save rate ≥30% (Athletic Greens benchmark from decoder bank), (2) monthly churn ≤8%, (3) pause option exists self-serve in account portal (legal CA + EU). Below threshold = default = one-time. Brand can opt-in subscription-default after hitting all 3 metrics in retention dashboard.

options.label: Just cancel rate ≤8% monthly
options.description: Single metric. Misses save-flow effectiveness signal.

options.label: Cancel-flow save ≥25% only
options.description: Save-flow signal. Ignores total churn rate.

options.label: Brand decides regardless of metrics
options.description: Pure delegation. Risks high-churn brands using sub-default and bleeding.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-005 — Cart-abandon trigger. Min cart value to fire recovery sequence?

options.label: AOV-derived: min = 0.6×median-AOV (apparel $30 / supplements $20 / beauty $18 / CPG $12 / home $45) (Recommended)
options.description: Below 0.6×median-AOV = abandoned cart not worth recovery effort (low LTV per email send + spam-filter risk). Apparel median $50 → min $30. Supplements $35 → $20. Beauty $30 → $18. CPG $20 → $12. Home $75 → $45. Per-niche tier matches free-ship formula consistency.

options.label: Universal $30 minimum across all niches
options.description: Simpler. Wrong for low-AOV CPG ($30 = above median for some CPG).

options.label: Universal $50 minimum (skill-file default)
options.description: Higher bar. Loses cart-abandon recovery for low-AOV niches entirely.

options.label: No minimum — always fire on any cart
options.description: Maximum recovery surface. Email volume + spam-filter hits + low ROI.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-006 — Post-purchase 1-click upsell. Complementary-only or replacement allowed?

options.label: Complementary ONLY (e.g., socks with shoes, conditioner with shampoo); never replacement-product upsells (Recommended)
options.description: Decoder-validated rule: Athletic Greens upsells GREENS+ enhancer (complementary). Allbirds upsells socks (complementary). Bombas upsells different sock pack-size (complementary). Replacement upsells (different mattress with same use-case as just-bought mattress) feel manipulative + risk return. Eligibility: tag-related complement, NOT same-category competitor product.

options.label: Replacement allowed if higher-AOV than cart
options.description: Maximum upsell aggression. Manipulative; risks return + brand trust erosion.

options.label: Same-category higher-AOV (replacement upsell)
options.description: Common ecom anti-pattern. Decoder bank shows it underperforms complementary.

options.label: Brand decides per product catalog
options.description: Pure delegation.
